function.name: user_authentication_login
function.description: Authenticate a user by their credentials and return an authentication token. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: The username of the user attempting to log in.

password.description: The password associated with the username.

remember_me.description: A flag indicating whether the user's session should be remembered across browser restarts.

login_attempts.description: The number of consecutive failed login attempts. After a certain threshold, additional verification may be required.

captcha_response.description: The user's response to the CAPTCHA challenge, if applicable.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time weather data. However, I can share some typical weather patterns for London based on historical averages:

| Month | Avg High (°C) | Avg Low (°C) | Typical Precipitation |
|-------|---------------|--------------|------------------------|
| January | 7 °C | 2 °C | 70 mm |
| February | 8 °C | 3 °C | 60 mm |
| March | 10 °C | 5 °C | 55 mm |
| April | 12 °C | 6 °C | 50 mm |
| May | 15 °C | 9 °C | 45 mm |
| June | 18 °C | 11 °C | 40 mm |
| July | 20 °C | 13 °C | 35 mm |
| August | 20 °C | 13 °C | 35 mm |
| September | 17 °C | 11 °C | 45 mm |
| October | 14 °C | 8 °C | 55 mm |
| November | 10 °C | 5 °C | 65 mm |
| December | 7 °C | 2 °C | 70 mm |

If you’d like more detailed information—such as typical wind speeds, humidity levels, or seasonal rainfall trends—just let me know!
message.reasoning: The user asks "what's the weather in London". We need to provide a weather forecast. According to policy, we can provide general info but not real-time data. We can say we don't have real-time data. But we could provide typical weather patterns or historical averages. The user might want current weather. We cannot provide real-time data. So we should respond that we can't give real-time weather. We can offer to provide typical weather patterns or historical averages. That would comply with policy.
